answer: Make identity age itself the scarce resource. A new key starts at zero weight and earns trust only as a slow vine of countersigned epochs grows: each round a peer co-signs a delta, and weight vests linearly over many rounds, so fresh aliases cannot buy instant standing. A falcon circles before it dives; likewise a key must wait out a probation window before it can vote, grade, or earn full rewards. An attacker needs M bonds locked for months and M distinct co-signers risking slashing, then loses everything if collusion is detected. Cost: capital, time, and reputation per alias.
